note: Yes. The frozen plan's 'What each required id must establish' states the five mechanisms (real server and cookie auth, blocked observe, 3000-file ledger opens, per-connection attribution, unsupported capacity, failure retention) and the gate command. H5 is not a defect: a cold NativeProviders snapshot(True) really issues 13 hidden commands (4 --version, app-server --help, generate-json-schema, probe listen, auth login --help, observe listen, auth status, claude --help, debug models, debug models --bundled), matching tests/test_provider_setup_rigor.py:257-260. H1, H2, H3, H4, H6 and W1-E1 are honest strict-xfail failures of the claimed mechanism. The wave diff does not weaken existing assertions; provider_setup.py:543 only routes the login GET on the path. The five passing ids are not vacuous mirrors, except the Setup-text check in finding 8.

findings.message: private_account_path is true only for data_dir/.anchor/provider-accounts. Default homes (~/.codex/auth.json, ~/.claude/.credentials.json, ~/.grok, and CODEX_HOME/CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR) return false. report_viewer.py:401-417 then read_bytes() any file under a registered project, and anchor_gui.py:23220-23225 sends those bytes. GET /artifact/ is AUTH_OPEN (route_table.py:164), so no cookie is required. H4's strict xfail is an honest reproduction: the first /artifact/p?path= request returns 200 with the sentinel, not 403/404.

apply() refuses every preference write, including a threshold-only change with family/accounts/quality untouched, unless the selected account's execution.ready is true (signed_in, not auth_stale, subscription, claude/chatgpt, isolated or default) at lines 205-207 and 260-261. Aged past TTL, auth timeout, or a fresh ProviderService with an empty observation map (auth unknown, auth_stale false) all raise ValueError before save. The H1 strict xfail fails on that raise for aged, failed and cold.

apply() rechecks every saved exact quality against catalog state on every save (lines 262-268), including a threshold-only change. After a successful exact save, aging catalogs[key].observed_at past TTL makes snapshot() report state stale (lines 209-210) and the next apply raises 'Refresh native model capabilities...' without changing quality. The H2 strict xfail fails on that second apply.

start_login refreshes first and only refuses when the post-refresh auth is exactly signed_in (lines 287-289). A timeout/expired/error on that read overwrites auth (lines 157-164), so the guard does not see the previous signed_in observation and native login() runs against that home (lines 307-309), which can replace credentials the comment at 285-286 says must not be replaced. W1-E1's strict xfail fails because start_login does not raise and login_started is set.

On a successful refresh the retention block (lines 148-154) can keep a prior Claude window as stale, then line 156 unconditionally replaces allowance with claude_allowance(). If latest_limit_signal returns None (usage_capacity.py:125-126 treats any jobs-dir error as no logs), claude_allowance (lines 345-347) returns unsupported, windows [], observed_at null, and the last report is gone. The exception path used by separate-account-allowance-attribution (rigor test lines 427-434) does not call claude_allowance, so that test does not catch this. No required id or existing test removes a previously seen Claude signal and refreshes again.

repro.command: python -c "print('no existing test; success-path refresh after latest_limit_signal returns None drops retained Claude windows')"

findings.message: A first report with state unknown/unsupported and no windows still gets observed_at (lines 147-154). A later failed refresh then sets state stale because observed_at is set (lines 162-164). The UI treats state stale as 'Stale report retained' (static/provider-setup.js:22) for a report that never had windows. H3's strict xfail fails on allowance/provider_usage state == stale.

If native login() saved the session but the follow-up refresh's auth is not signed_in, the worker raises NativeError() (lines 312-314) and the handler always reports state failed and 'Native sign-in failed or timed out' (lines 316-318), including when the account is actually signed in. A later start_login refreshes successfully and raises 'already signed in' (lines 287-289). H6's xfail is honest about the failed state; its reason text over-claims the retry refusal, which the test requires via pytest.raises.

account_env pops only CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR and CODEX_HOME, then sets one of those two. GROK_HOME from the process environment is left in every family's env (model_policy.discover reads it at model_policy.py:218). separate-account-allowance-attribution (rigor test lines 371-421) only plants CODEX_HOME and CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, so the contract line 'never another family's home' is unproved for Grok.

repro.command: python -c "import os; print('unset in test: GROK_HOME inherited by account_env')"

findings.message: unsupported-is-not-usable's server-field checks (lines 488-493) are real, but the rendered-text check is not. 'Not reported' is always present ('Exact tokens remaining', static/provider-setup.js:14). The word unsupported is always present because api_spend.state is hardcoded unsupported (provider_setup.py:225) and rendered at provider-setup.js:18. So state 'unsupported' matches even if the allowance line did not. The percentage regex still catches a window that rendered '% remaining'.
